items.text: This is it. The final lap.

When we launched Redout 2, we wanted to build the fastest, the most unforgiving, the most alive antigravity racer ever made. What we didn’t expect was you: the speedrunners shaving milliseconds off World Records at 3 AM, the tournament organizers running brackets on their own time, the modders, the Discord regulars, the people who kept coming back to the same corner of Fuji until they could take it blindfolded.

Every patch since launch was built on your emotions, your bug reports, your clips and your comebacks. We listened, and we kept tuning, because a community this dedicated deserved a game that could keep up.

So for our last update, we’re not slowing down. We’re giving you a new mode built for competitions, unlocking hundreds more parts so every ship on the grid is unmistakably yours, and cleaning up everything we could find along the way.
Consider it our thank you, and our hand-off: from here on, the track belongs to you.
See you at the finish line and on the next start grid. Which may be sooner than you can reasonably expect.
Pazzi e indomabili.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41628290/c618a16e40fcea9938d05b676c3b5247f1e9d46e.png"]

We love the ideas you come up with as a community, especially if it comes to custom event rulesets. One of our programmers liked the “Burnout” tournament mechanics so much that he just decided in his spare time to implement it as a whole new gamemode!

Introducing: “Rush” and “Boss Rush” - A series of races on your selected tracks (or environments), drawn at random. The last racer of each race is eliminated until only one remains. After the first race, the starting grid follows the final rank of the previous one.

The group leader selects a deck of tracks, creating a pool that the game will randomly draw from for the duration of the event. After playing one track, it is removed from the pool until no tracks remain. Then, the pool gets reshuffled. Eliminated Racers become Spectators (outside of the standard Spectator limit) and can watch the rest of the event unfold from the front-row seats!
These gamemodes are available in private lobbies only.

Unlocked 766 more aesthetic parts for all ships in total. You can find all of them in the garage from the get-go. It took us way too long to sort out the logistics of this, but I mean… There are a lot of parts!
“Suspend when Unfocused” now also mutes all game sounds and pauses played cutscenes. Shhh…
Fixed held boost input sometimes not activating after using a Rewind.
Added a link to our Discord in the Main Menu to let you connect with our community Faster Than Ever!
Added possibility of creating groups while already being in a public online lobby. No need to leave to invite friends anymore!
Removed “Privacy and Data Collection” and third-party EULA agreements front the game because we no longer collect any data outside of one covered by platform EULAs.

Added the possibility of replaying Environment and Ship introduction cutscenes, in Arcade gamemode options and during prerace, respectively. We put an insane amount of time, effort and love into those… And then let you watch them only once!
Grounded flying speed pads on Fuji and Mariana Trench environments.
Polished polish translation and fixed its wrong ordinal numbers’ punctuation. Now polish is polished. Ostatnio jak sprawdzałem, Merkury nie był księżycem. Pierogi też są dobre.
Increased base top speed of all ships by around 3%. Some could dare to say, you can now be… Faster Than Ever!
Increased speed gain on negative-G track sections (while providing correct pitch down input, of course).
Improved general multiplayer stability.
Fixed first race in a public online lobby always being 1-lap long.
Fixed lobbies being created with less than two racers. One racer races didn’t feel fair to us.
Fixed race countdown sound effects playing for the second time for lobby clients.
Fixed possibility of starting a race while still looking at the track from prerace cameras.
Group Leader can be now a Spectator, but only in Private matches.
Fixed groups sometimes being destroyed on return to the menu from online races. Now friends can stay friends.
Fixed a softlock for group clients if the leader lost connection to a public lobby host.
Raised privileges of cameramen to allow them to automatically use Follow-Offset cameras randomly in places where standard auto-broadcast used to just point at a wall.
Improved camera stability in Spline mode with Look-At enabled on ship closeups.
Fixed jittering field of view in Follow mode after a race restart.
Fixed Speed and Roll visual bars not showing up after race restart in Arcade Spectator.
Spline Look-At has now a “Reset” button. This feature puts the camera 30 meters behind the focused ship.
Raised maximum camera speed for Spline and Free modes.
Spectators now can see the track name and its direction before the start of the race, as well as in the Pause Menu.
Improved movement and rotation of the Free camera while tracking players.
Fixed menu appearance of groups larger than 12.
Fixed sorting spectators and racers in the online multiplayer player list.
Moved the cutscene subtitles above the black bar to avoid clipping with the “Skip” button.
Fixed environmental sounds not playing on the first loop of pre-race cinematic cameras showcasing the environment.
Fixed race music not starting properly after quitting from a previous event during a big jump.
Fixed big jump windup sound effect continuing to play in the Main Menu after quitting a multiplayer game at a specific point.
Skill :P
Some game localizations have minor text clipping.
Lunare is still not the best team in the game…
Many very minor issues that bother us that you may or may not have ever heard about.
This is the last update. We’re aware. We’re not okay about it either. We hope therapy will help us all.
Or maybe we’ll do another one at some point, who knows?

Ten years in and we're still not done with Redout. This time it's not just about racing, it's about watching… Spectator Mode has landed: you can now sit back, grab a camera, and watch online and Arcade races like a proper SRRL broadcaster. It's our thank you to everyone who's been streaming tournaments with zero official tools all these years. And since we were already in the garage, we raised the grid to 34 ships (totally random number, don't ask), had a serious talk with a certain propulsor brand, and fixed a pile of things along the way. Hope you appreciate and enjoy it!
It is now possible to watch online and Arcade races using a brand-new Spectator Mode!
This feature is a love letter to the community of great players that currently find ways to stream their multiplayer games and tournaments without any official tool to help.
How to access
In Arcade, select a supported mode (Race or Boss) and enable the Spectator Mode toggle. Adjust other settings to your liking, pick a track, and you’ll be thrown straight into the race.

In Online Races, either start matchmaking as you normally would, or join another friend’s group through an invite (unfortunately, neither party leader, nor lobby host are able to spectate). In both scenarios, you will be prompted to select a role; a Racer or a Spectator. Select the latter option and you’ll be ready to go!

A detailed guide on the usage and features of Spectator mode is going to be published later on Steam Community forums, in a pinned thread. Here’s a brief overview of what can be done (dang, I wrote this like an AI there, but I promise, I am human):

After loading into the race, you’ll start in the Broadcast mode. This mode lets you automatically follow the focused ship around the track, looking at it from various cameras placed along the racetrack. The view can be changed to the player’s perspective, also with an option of offsetting the camera. Change the focus to a different player either by opening the player list and selecting the desired player, or typing their position on the keyboard, using 0-9 keys (positions over 9th are also selectable, just wait for a while before providing the number). You can also use an option to follow the race leader. Camera will change automatically with that option enabled.

At any point during the spectated race, the camera can be detached to enter the Free flight mode. In this mode, the only boundaries are collisions with objects, so you can go nuts! (Touching the sun is not recommended.)
From Free flight, you can access the Spline mode, which attaches the camera to the closest active track piece to fly along it with limited offset.
We can’t wait to see what you can cook up with these brand-new possibilities of capturing fully cinematic gameplay footage!
Other New Features
On queuing up for a Multiplayer race or upon joining a group, it is now possible to choose if you want to be a spectator or a racer.
Added a new option to set a maximum racer (2-34) and spectator (0-6) amount for the multiplayer lobby (applicable from the next hosted session). Default values are 12 and 4 respectively.
Added a new option to set a maximum number of full-quality opponents rendered on the screen at the same time (set it lower for better performance in crowded offline and online races).
Added a new option to disable “OVERHEAT” notification from appearing on the middle of the screen.
Added an option to erase best Time Attack times on the local leaderboard. Find it on the pre-race scene of the selected track in Time Attack game mode.

SRRL found a concerning amount of inconsistencies across many signature ship parts and decided to take action to even out the field, especially in a field of propulsors. One certain brand had an outstanding advantage in the engine department, hiding its unfair practices from the technical inspectors for years. As a penalty, said propulsor hasn’t received any upgrades, while all others got a substantial buff to catch up to the same level.

Departments of the teams providing highest-tier rudders were ashamed of the fact that off-brand parts were always performing better than their signature counterparts for so long. As a result of additional funding, they significantly reduced the drawbacks of their parts.
All balance changes are listed below.
Increased Conqueror’s thrust.
Increased Mantis’ stability.
Increased Lunare’s top speed and stability, decreased steering.
Significantly increased top speed of all but Lunare’s Signature Propulsors and slightly bumped up Mantis Propulsor’s thrust. Minor adjustments to the penalties of the changed propulsors.
Increased steer and strafe performance of Signature Rudders and lowered penalties applied by them, while still staying true to the part characteristics from their description.
Increased top speed of Koeniggswerth’s and Behemoth’s Signature Hulls.
Decreased top speed penalty for Koeniggswerth’s and Behemoth’s Signature Intercoolers.
Decreased stability penalty for Buran’s Signature Intercooler.
Increased stability for Lunare’s and Koeniggswerth’s E.S.C.s.
Decreased hull penalty for Lunare’s and Mantis’ E.S.C.s.
Decreased top speed penalty for Koeniggswerth’s E.S.C.
Increased strafe for Lunare’s and Asera’s E.S.C.s.
Raised max power level cap of highest-tier career events from 1200 to 1300.

After a long and careful investigation, SRRL haven’t found evidence of Mantis Propulsor being a stolen property of the Buran engine development team. As a result, their propulsor is correctly labelled as “PSMA” now.
Updated Lunare’s Signature Propulsor power ranking to reflect its true value (238 -> 274).
More pilots have qualified to the elite SRRL league! You might even be able to recognize some of them.
Bent spacetime slightly more to fix track previews, descriptions and thumbnails shifted by one on Origin Black Hole. Singularity is no joke, even for the UI.
Fixed a rare softlock on the game mode change overlay, in Arcade track selection.
Fixed one of the mini-winglets of ‘Wing’ flaps cosmetic part for Akhal-Tech twisting in the wrong direction when accelerating.
Fixed ‘Airblade Gen II’ auxiliary cosmetic part for Sulha promoting vector strafing on boosting.
Fixed missing translation of “create group” prompt in the main menu.
Raised the possible maximum number of ships in Arcade races from 12 to 34 (higher values WILL hurt the performance, especially on the race start, overdo it at your own risk).
Improved position and visible ship status correction for the opponent players, to smooth out the multiplayer experience for both racers and spectators.
Fixed some infinite loading scenarios while loading into the race for the first time in the play session.
Options and Group Menu are now accessible on the prerace screen, before entering the garage.
Fixed "Desolation Ring" and its author not being displayed on the pre-race scene. It’s not desolated anymore.
Fixed wrong power level displayed after using a saved loadout on a ship with a different base power level.
Improved the behavior and appearance of offscreen opponent indicators (thanks Dandy!)
Hid non-relevant information about session best lap time on the UI in Time Attack game mode.
Times set in Qualifying gamemode no longer are saved to the local Time Attack leaderboard.
Hid the personal best time on the Qualifying results screen.
Enabled Checkpoint time splits in Training and Time Attack game modes.

Checkpoint time splits in Time Attack are now compared to the time splits of your best recorded lap. Times recorded before this update have no checkpoint split data to be compared to, so no delta will be displayed.
Added a checkered flag background for the opponents who have finished the race before the player.

Back so soon? You bet! 1.3.3 is a quick pit stop: a handful of fixes for timers, multiplayer results and one embarrassingly blurry logo. We'd rather get them to you now than make you wait. But something bigger is on the way for the coming weeks!
Fixed some edge cases with boost input not being applied after closing Pause Menu or using Rewind.
Fixed all (or we truly hope so) instances of end event time sometimes being increased by 1 millisecond. THIS CHANGES EVERYTHING.
Fixed 34BigThings’ logo being blurry and pixelated in the game intro cutscene. Now, we guarantee you, it’s much better.
Fixed end results not counting time of unraced laps to the total race time after hot-joining post-first lap.
Fixed end results sometimes showing finishers in the wrong order. Bribed personnel have been exiled to the Origin Black Hole.
Gave coffee to the stopwatch guy so the race timer for clients doesn’t start with a delay anymore.
Fixed a rare crash for party members caused by failing to load the “Welcome” map after the host left the lobby before the race started. As you know, you are welcome here any time.
Fixed a very rare issue of having only the engine trails visible for the opponents after destroying the ship during the race.
Changed color of the game version number in credits to white (red is out…)
Fixed offroad SFX emitted by the opponents being played, heard from too far away, and never being stopped.
We continue to monitor the overall possible pace in various tracks with the recent changes in pitching behavior.
Rarely, race countdown SFX might be replayed for lobby clients just after the race start.
Part of the “Spirit’s Peak” music track plays with the music off.

Hi everyone, it has been a long time! And we are pretty sure a Redout 2 update in late 2026 wasn’t in your bingo card, as it has not been on ours for a long time as well! But today Redout turns 10 years old and we wanted to do something special, weird… and full of love for our game.

In addition to the surprise update to Redout 2, we wanted to announce our partnership with Antidote Games to create a tabletop experience for the Redout universe. We've taken over your screens, but now we're targeting your tables! The team at Antidote Games brings deep experience in physical game design, and together we are translating the high-speed energy of Redout into a physical format.
We mean latest, not last ;)

But we had a lot of fixes and improvements we wanted to make for this game and we finally had the chance to put our hands on it. Hope you enjoy the renewed stability of version 1.3.2 with a total of 174 changes, some details here:
It is now possible to skip most cinematics (intro movies, env reveals, team reveals…).
Added a toggle to the Options allowing to suspend the game processes when it is not focused (Off by default), which improves the performance.
Hired an elite pest control team and erased all landing bugs from existence.
Various performance improvements, you will notice the difference specifically on AMD and Snapdragon X Elite chipsets.
Pitch was frame dependent. Now it’s a grown adult that can live on its own.
Along with pitch frame dependency, the side-effect of gaining extra speed on traversing loops has been patched as well.
Added a mechanic of gaining extra speed on traversing loops.
Fixed game introduction cinematic clip.
Fixed Custom assists not being immediately applied if changed during the race, not that many will notice, but still…
AI opponents now drive more consistently and explode less on tricky jumps on higher difficulties.
Fixed a softlock on changing application focus at a certain moment during the first game start. Keep your focus on Redout.
Fixed a common crash on event completion if Photo Mode and high graphics preset was used during it. Photo Mode only deserved Ultra and you know it.
Fixed loss of button focus on re-focusing the game in Photo Mode.
Fixed ships attempting to make a chin photo closeup impression after finishing the race if first person view is used.
Fixed various camera post-process effects being still active after a race restart.
Fixed tutorial slow motion being applied to the camera view transition.
Fixed tutorial messages staying on screen forever in some cases.
Fixed game automatically pausing on the race countdown if a controller was connected during the loading.
Disabled controller vibration if keyboard is used as an input device.
Disabled controller input if the game is not focused.
Smoothened camera transition on entering and exiting the Rewind state.
Various fixes and improvements of camera movement for the ship inspection mode in the garage.
Fixed no longer provided input being active after resuming the race.
Fixed ship drift lightning visual effect rendering higher and higher after each quick restart.
Fixed animated object collisions being desynchronised with visual appearance after usage of a Rewind.
Slightly increased default gamepad deadzone.
Improved the driving skills of an autopilot taking control over the player’s ship after a completed race.
Crossing the finish line while in overheat explosion state (but before exploding for good) now correctly triggers it. Basically fireworks.
Fixed an exploit letting the player manually respawn on any track piece with a clever usage and combination of using Rewind and exploding. “Clever”.
Fixed ship exploding on Rewind confirmation if Rewind has been activated while taking damage from Missed Landing.
Fixed ship instantly exploding on Rewind confirmation at any point during the overheat death sequence
Fixed an exploit involving Rewinds, allowing the player to stay in a destroyed state forever. Not sure why anyone would want to do that but okay.
Raised health warning sound start from 20% to 25% to allow low-hull-high-thrust ship pilots to have a chance to react while boost stacking.

Installed new magnets (we’re still not sure how they work) in all ships, which resulted in going through the loops without scrapping the ground and negative-g loops without detaching at extreme speeds, as long as the correct input is provided of course.
Fixed Boost Safety assist forgetting that it would be nice if it could cancel Hyperboost activation while at max heat and at health safety limit.
Fixed a rare instance of ships surviving an upside-down landing. Not sure if physically accurate.
Fixed various ways of accessing Rewind and Pause Menu shortly after crossing the finish line.
Added Boss mode to Online Private lobbies.
Raised the DNF timer from 30 to 60 seconds.
Fixed the possibility of being put on a wrong track after hot-joining the running race under specific scenarios.
Status of the players on the Player List now always correctly says “Racing” instead of “Ready” while the race is underway.
Improved the accuracy of opponent’s state representation in online races. No more mind-blowing sound effects from everyone around on repeat!
Fixed an issue with ship being able to be launched into space on collision with many ships at once.
Improved player distance tracking quality.
Matchmaking can’t be cancelled by accident on a loading screen anymore.
Fixed a rare occurrence of missing UI after loading into a multiplayer race.
Fixed an ultra-rare issue of the lobby host starting the race on Cloud Ocean with maximum heat and zero health (Now it’s maximum health and zero heat for the record).
The game now informs you whenever a group leader disbands their group in any way instead of moving every party member to the main menu without any explanation.
Fixed ship visibly spawning on the pole position for a brief moment after readying up.
Consulted Origin Black Hole specialists and fixed a time dilation which caused lobby clients to have a slower-working race timer than it should.
Fixed an issue of not being able to re-join the same multiplayer lobby after force-quitting the game from the race results screen beforehand.
Found a lost finish line flagman on a certain rock of Aura Reverse. Not sure how he has survived this long, but he’s been moved to the correct place. We call him Ulysses now.
As a result of the issue above, part of Time Attack leaderboards on Aura Reverse has been wiped.
Fixed jump windup sound effect being played on respawn from a failed jump at 41% of lap progression of Voyager Reverse
Fixed offroad effects affecting the ship on restarts from specific parts of Mars tracks.
Fixed “Trials of the Forest” (late A league) having impossible platinum time, git gud wasn’t enough.
Fixed wrong German translation of “Finish at X speed or faster” trophy.
Fixed an exploit allowing to get “Fly for X distance in a single jump” trophy on any jump.
Fixed wrong distance shown between player and the opponents on starting grid of some Boss tracks
Fixed main menu being visible in the background of league selection after finishing a career event
Fixed frozen ship stat comparison on travelling between Arcade and Career garages
Fixed Speed event trophy wrongly shown as unlocked without getting any medals
Fixed B League unlock popup appearing each time after finishing Class B Promotion Contest
Fixed Flight UI not disappearing at the end of first time user experience if it was completed mid-air
Fixed Flight UI displaying wrong inputs right after rebinding them
Fixed Wrong Way notification being visible shortly after respawning in some cases
Fixed Top 50 leaderboards tab showing more than 50 entries
Fixed “Top 5%” ranking being displayed instead of “Top 50%” in the leaderboards. Sorry, you still have a long way to go!
Fixed various visual bugs related to the state of Hyperboost.
Fixed “Create party” hint showing up when already in a party.
Fixed icons of clients not being loaded if they have joined the party later than the affected person. Icons of non-friended players still don’t load sometimes though. Beware of strangers.
Fixed “Share” button on controllers having a wrong icon.
Added more friends to the credits.
Fixed game music becoming muffled and stuck on certain sections each time after restarting a Time Attack event from the results screen.
Fixed game music being stuck on “bridge” section in Arena and Last Man Standing modes played against one opponent.
Removed speakers transmitting race sounds from the ship unlock garage.
Fixed offroad travel sound effects not being played after landing or respawning.
Just writing this here to remind ourselves the audio in this game was amazing and we are very proud of it.

We are aware of the fact that changes to the pitch behavior can render some world records in Time Attacks impossible to beat, but be assured that we are going to monitor the situation and react accordingly with slight buffs if needed. As stated before, this update is “latest”, not last :)
Offroad SFX often can get stuck playing when it shouldn’t on Reverse Boss tracks
Party members can very rarely encounter a game crash if the party leader has left the multiplayer race before it have started.

Well, we finally have some good news to share. We acquired back rights for Redout 2 and while we are eternally grateful to Saber Interactive for all the work done together, we couldn’t wait to get it back and restart some work on it.
As a thank you gift for all the patience and for having played Redout 2 since the beginning, we are shipping free content with this patch and a bunch of QoL fixes!
Three new tracks have been added to the V.E.R.T.E.X. environment, all playable in Arcade and Multiplayer. To some of you they might feel very familiar, let us know what you think!

Due to changes in tracks’ boundaries and ships’ behavior during development, with this patch we are cleaning up all times submitted to the Time Attack leaderboards, as well as players’ local best results.
Fixed rare crash on confirming rewind and on opening pause menu. Please stop trying to break it now.
Fixed an issue with players getting stuck upon entering the group menu from the loadout inspection screen. Same as above.
Fixed an issue with players getting stuck in Training mode when trying to start a training session and enter the garage at the same time. Bilocation is not supported in this universe, sorry.
Fixed garage flow break upon attempting to change the ship's aesthetics while spectating it. It’s rude, at least close your eyes!
Spreaded some soil on Mars Memorial. No more digging your ship into the ground and spinning like a beyblade there!
Removed a barrier protecting the rock on the split path jump of Tropical Twister Forward. The rock is adult now, it can handle destroying ships itself!
Located scrap collectors who occasionally stole loose track pieces from some Boss tracks. We made sure that this won’t happen anymore.
Fixed ships having too high top speed after using a quick restart from underwater and at the beginning of every event on the Origin Black Hole tracks.
Fixed multiplayer lap times being saved as local Time Attack records.
Adjusted power levels and unlocking conditions for some trials.
Added an option to toggle Motion Blur (applied while boosting).
Fixed various minor translation mistakes in different languages.
Removed unused items from the game menu.
Trees no longer appear on track in the distance on Mars tracks
Hired more laser snipers for patrolling pilots attempting to gain an unfair advantage by leaving the track. As a result, over 210 unwanted shortcuts have been removed from the game.
Reintroduced a small damage threshold before disrupting health regeneration and its cooldown.
Fixed turbo pads sometimes not activating at high speeds and low FPS.
Fixed an issue with the ship not receiving a landing boost if the previous landing was performed within the last 2 seconds.
Fixed an issue with the ship rarely not receiving landing boost on good and perfect landings.
Fixed an issue with ships rarely taking damage on good and perfect landings.
Fixed an issue with ships sometimes slowing down too much on all landings.
Fixed an issue with ships sometimes detaching immediately after landing.
Fixed an issue with ships falling through the track while landing near its edges.
Unified shapes and rotation of all ships’ floor collision boxes.
Added visible countdown timer to race’s end in multiplayer races.
Extended time to finish the multiplayer race to 30 seconds.
Shortened time for the lobby host to select the next track. However, now opening the track selection screen freezes the countdown.
"Elements of Storms" event now correctly rewards the players with the “Autumn” color scheme. We moved the “Summer” color to the Winter League to counter climate change.
Set correct platinum medal score requirement for “Sakura Rush” campaign event.
Adjusted trophy difficulty for the “Paradise Island” event and the first one of “Conqueror Strong Ship Tournament”.
Career trophy's progress is now visible in pause menu
Fixed “Redout Grandmaster” requiring the player to complete DLC campaigns.
Fixed “Fashion Racer” requiring the player to also unlock aesthetics from Caribbean Dam DLC.
Added “Racer’s Home” environmental variations also to non-tournament campaign garages.
The .mp3 version of “Desolation Ring” in the OST is no longer “Sledge” track.

items.text: Get ready to brave the latest venue in Redout 2's second DLC: the Terror Rupes of Mercury! This environment comes with three reversible tracks and their boss version, exclusive aesthetic components and new Career events! The patch also includes a brand-new Training Mode that allows players to play an infinite number of laps on any track they want in order to hone their skills!
Watch the Winter Pack DLC trailer here!
Here’s a scorching-hot list of everything included in this patch:
Introducing “Terror Rupes”! This harsh environment switches heat for cold and back again without any notice
Introducing Training mode, an infinite Time Attack mode where you can test out tracks, ships and loadouts
Added a new low health warning sound effect. Also, its volume level is now adjustable in Settings
Missing a landing while auto-healing or at full health now correctly destroys the ship
Caribbean Dam and Mount Fuji have been optimized for better performance
Fixed impossible to obtain trophy in The Waterflow Dance tournament
Fixed softlocks in garage while using the Group menu
Player is now able to cross the finish line while being last in Arena Race event
Fixed an endless sound riser on Tropical Twister
Additional performance optimizations
Fixed an issue that potentially caused a softlock on the Reward screen in the Career when pressing Tab
Fixed an issue that caused track progress to be reset to 0% when missing the last jump in Mars Memorial - Orbiter
Fixed playerlist width being resized while readying up in multiplayer match in Russian
Fixed first person and chase camera sometimes being stuck inside the ship
Countdown number no longer stays on the screen after using a quick restart
Fixed an issue that caused the incorrect soundtrack name to be displayed when Streamer mode is enabled
Fixed old in-race notifications all showing up after turning Screen HUD on
Changed requirements making it easier to unlock some tutorial levels
Arcade ships; Asera, Behemot, Wallace, ESA, Sulha, Lunare have received a buff, with Asera and Behemoth receiving a major one, and Wallace, ESA, Sulha and Lunare getting a minor one
Updated the hot and cold sections visual representation on screen
Changed behavior of inactive track segments. Now, they destroy the ship on contact
Slightly tweaked visuals of inactive tracks. Now they’re easier to recognise
Game can occasionally crash at the end of a race when playing or using photo mode with graphic preset set to High
In some trials, an arcade ship under the required power level is automatically selected
In some rare cases the rewind feature doesn’t work as expected in Training mode
Arcade Asera got so fast with its buff that it lost its windshield texture
Lap times from multiplayer races are mistakenly saved to local best “Time Trials”
Potential soft-lock interaction between garage and race-start in Practice mode
Redout Grandmaster and Fashion Racer achievements unlock criteria wrongly require DLC events completion

topNew: Introducing “Terror Rupes”! This harsh environment switches heat for cold and back again without any notice

Added a new low health warning sound effect. Also, its volume level is now adjustable in Settings

items.text: Unlocked 72 new aesthetic modules
Fixed multiplayer issues with wrong gravity, top speed and heat generation on all environments
Fixed Thrust stat not behaving correctly and not applying the correct speed gain
Steering stat adjusted to increase turn speed and turn rate whilst braking
Tweaked bonus trophies in Career mode which were hard to obtain
Fixed bug with manual respawn which places the playership in the wrong place on the track in Time Attack
Fixed descriptions not matching event contents in Summer League
Rebalanced Career Time Attack and Speed goals to match new changes in Thrust and Steering
Underwater now shows cooling VFX for clarity
If you're experiencing an issue, be sure to check out known issues page current updates: https://support.saber.games/hc/en-us/articles/8174504112913

items.text: It’s finally time to showcase our first DLC for Redout 2, featuring a complete new location: Caribbean Dam! This environment comes with three reversible tracks and their boss version, exclusive aesthetic components and the dolphin-like experience you never knew you wanted to try in Redout!
Watch our latest trailer here!
Added the ability to choose lap count for all races in private multiplayer sessions
Added Quick Restart option to Time Attack races
Added a new widget to display the music track played during races
100+ aesthetic rewards have now been unlocked
Fixed an issue with players sometimes clipping through the tracks on Tartarus
Fixed the naming of rewards being misleading after the completion of a race
Fixed players being kicked out from groups during multiplayer races
Fixed instances where assisted controls are not behaving correctly on reverse tracks
Fixed an exploit where AI ships crash immediately on Cloud Ocean - Mistral Reverse
Additional performance optimizations
Fixed instances where achievements were not unlocking for:
Fashion Racer
Try them all
Sweats Profusely
Grand Slam
Improvements to track design and signage on parts of Tartarus
Time Attack and Speed times further refined in the campaign to be more accessible
Added a new UI element in track select that indicates the length of track the player is about to race in (Short, Medium, Long, Extra Long)
Additional UI and UX improvements to the Photo Mode feature set
The campaign rewards UI now displays what team each reward is for
Added new effects when your craft is affected by environmental temperatures
Added option to disable Kinetic lines in the Options
Asera power unit has moved backwards
There is a chance that timers will display “.000” incorrectly in certain circumstances
Extremely rare chance to crash when client joins a multiplayer game whilst the map changes
Some track segments when inactive sometimes show no lighting instead of glowing red
In some multiplayer situations gravity will act strangely in Marianna and Caribbean Dam
Some event descriptions in the Caribbean Dam campaign don't match their content
Tree LODs can sometimes clip inside the track

We’ve discovered an issue preventing the correct upload of entries to the Leaderboards and metadata in Arcade mode. This caused several visualization errors in both Loadouts and Power Levels.
This should be resolved in today's Hotfix 1.0.6 while we work on a bigger patch for version 1.1.0!

Fixes to correctly upload time records on the Leaderboards in Arcade Mode. Keep in mind that Time Records obtained while playing in Career Mode are not uploaded to the Leaderboards due to the Power Level differences between events on the same track.
Fixes to upload the correct Leaderboards metadata (Loadout, Power levels, etc.)

Redout 2 is not meant to be an easy game. The skill ceiling is high by design and we want players to feel challenged. At the same time, we also have a series of Auto Calibration systems so casual players can enjoy the game as well.
With that said, Redout 2 launched with a steeper level of difficulty than we had intended and below in patch 1.0.4 are some changes to help make that better.
Boosting thresholds have been adjusted for Silver and Bronze in the Rookie Academy.
Various tweaks have been made depending on the level of difficulty for each player. This does not affect Master or Nightmare difficulty.
Fixed the Auto Calibration Threshold difficulty assigned for each player depending on their race results.
